claims.text: High-temperature diffusion carburizing of Ti-6Al-4V will form a thin, continuous TiC surface layer.
A TiC surface layer produced by carburizing will significantly increase the surface hardness and wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V.
Untreated Ti-6Al-4V typically has a surface hardness of approximately 300-400 HV.
Untreated Ti-6Al-4V has relatively high wear rates under dry sliding conditions.
Exposure to a carbon-rich atmosphere at elevated temperature promotes in situ TiC formation on Ti-6Al-4V.
The proposed improvement should hold during room-temperature dry sliding at about 10 N load and 500 mm/s sliding velocity.
The improvement may extend to typical structural service environments.
Carburizing produces a continuous layer of fine or nanostructured TiC at the alloy surface.
A surface carbide-containing layer can act as a hard, wear-resistant barrier.
During carburizing, carbon diffuses into titanium and reacts with it to form chemically bonded TiC.
The TiC layer provides dispersion strengthening and limits surface plastic deformation.
Carbide reinforcement of a surface layer can increase hardness and reduce wear-related material loss.
Carburized Ti-6Al-4V will have approximately 30-40% greater surface hardness than untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Carburized Ti-6Al-4V will have approximately 50% lower wear rate than untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The beneficial effect depends on achieving an optimal diffusion depth and a uniform TiC layer.
Excessive or uneven carbide formation could make the treated surface brittle.
The improvement will vary with carburizing temperature, treatment time, carbon activity, load, sliding speed, and environment.
The treatment may involve a trade-off between increased surface hardness and reduced toughness.
